mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which is likely to boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the weakening labor market.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening economy, which is likely to boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) relative to its 12-month moving average indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and real GDP (GDPC1) is contracting, it signals a supply-side recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average and GDPC1 is contracting.
